# Hardening notes — hogee run-9

Hunter hardening notes kept in ledger bookkeeping (not findings; no verdicts). Grouped by hunter.

**h-cfo**

- cfo-guard: a proposal refused by recheck (e.g. agent revoked/expired) does not use its slot, so every pass (144/day plus one per sale wake) appends another DENY POLICY_VERDICT event to trace:cfo-guard:<day>:<slot> (cfo-guard.ts:129-143, 222-225); an alert-once check (store/trace.ts hasTrace) would bound it.
- core/cfo/ledger.ts:144-154: sampleDays counts days with recorded sales as well as spend, so DEMO_MODE test sales let burn detection (burn.ts:30, MIN_SAMPLE_DAYS 3) and therefore tightening start before three days of spend data exist; still tighten-only and one per line per day. Counting spend days only for burns would match the stated intent.
- packages/api/src/services/cfo.ts:273-296: the block-time cache is cleared wholesale at 20,000 entries and has no single-flight, so past 20,000 distinct record blocks (or on a cold start with concurrent requests) each GET /api/cfo refetches every block timestamp; GET /api/cfo also reads all-time payment and sale rows per request with no rate limit. An LRU plus a stored block_time column would bound it.
- packages/api/src/services/cfo.ts:304: committedPlanRow is read at the current DB state, not pinned to the snapshot block, so a replan landing after B can pair a newer manifest's stage gate with stage state at B (display only).
- apps/worker/src/jobs/cfo-guard-inputs.ts:76-80 and services/cfo.ts:219-223: auto_released is computed from current escrow_milestones state, not state at B (supplier-cost classification only; never used by tightening).
- cfo-guard pass has no overall deadline; pg-boss expiry (300 s) marks the job failed but the handler keeps the advisory lock until it returns.

**h-chat**

- packages/api/src/journey/text.ts:56-58: on the routed `plan` skill the router's LLM_CALL traces are committed in their own transaction (traceRouter) before plannerTurn, so a planner call refused by the model budget leaves those trace rows although the turn stores nothing else; fold them into plannerTurn's transaction or write them only after the planner succeeds.
- packages/api/src/http/rate-limit.ts:30-31: DEFAULT_CHAT_RATE assumes a turn makes up to PLANNER_MAX_STEPS (6) model calls, but a routed `plan` turn now makes the router call plus up to 6 planner calls (7); the model budget still caps total spend, but the sizing comment and per-turn estimate are stale.
- packages/core/src/journey/history.ts:72-73: tookEffect treats the last stored message as effective; a claimed press whose assistant reply failed to persist (an error after claim) keeps counting as a taken-effect pick or terms_saved until another message lands. journeyFactsOf re-filters picks against current facility candidates, so this has no authority effect.
- packages/api/src/journey/actions.ts:64: the stored user label comes from history.buttonLabel(action.actionId), so a client can resend a server-issued actionId with a different action body and the transcript shows the server's label for another action; transcript integrity only, as ids are re-checked. Consider requiring that a labelled actionId's stored action equals the pressed one.
- packages/api/src/journey/effects.ts:104-106: useCatalog invokes supplierRoutes.shortlistSuppliers directly with a server-built spec cast `as never`, bypassing the register layer's ShortlistBody parse and response validation; call startShortlist with a ShortlistSpec.parse'd spec instead.
- packages/api/src/services/chat-store.ts:80-104: memory entries are read per facility, not per session, so an answer stored in one client-chosen session shapes the planner in every other session of the facility; equivalent under the accepted anonymous-founder design, unchanged in this range.

**h-mock**

- packages/api-mock/src/features/orders.ts confirm lacks live's \p{Cf} refusal on holderName and bankName (packages/api/src/services/supplier-terms.ts 84-85); core FormText rejects only C0/DEL and holderMatchesSeller treats Cf characters as separators, so bidi/zero-width text reaches the 'Pays out to' row the founder signs. Same principal (founder form behind the Host/same-origin guard), so parity only.
- packages/api-mock/src/features/orders.ts has no MAX_TERMS_PER_WINDOW writer bound (live supplier-terms.ts 112); the in-memory terms map grows without a bound.
- packages/api-mock/src/features/search.ts startSearch checks IN_FLIGHT before `await runRecorded` and stores the job after it (238-241), so concurrent starts both run; live allows one in flight per process. Recorded data, no cost.
- packages/api-mock/src/features/search.ts overwrites web supplier rows in st.suppliers on every search (205); live supplier rows are insert-only. Recorded data are static today.
- packages/api-mock/src/features/cfo.ts serves the 14-day sample sales series in REPLAY mode too, but apps/web/components/cfo/cfo-model.ts dataLabel labels only mode 'mock' (and chainId 31337); with the fixtures' Sepolia chainId the replay CFO page shows fabricated sales, forecast and P&L without 'Sample data' (only the global 'Replay (offline)' badge).
- packages/api-mock/src/profile.ts MY settledSummary 'Test-mode payout succeeded; settlement confirmed on-chain' is applied to MOCK_ONLY web-supplier payments, which live pays through the simulated rail; label them 'simulated payout' like SG.
- Contract-example aliases: webSearchOf and getSupplierSearch serve the example READY search in the fresh scenario too, with createdAtMs = now (the 7-day age gate never applies), and the default-scenario submitOrderTerms returns the example CONFIRMED body when the exact example body fails its checks (orders.ts 273); never signable (termsId not stored).
- apps/web/scripts/dev-mock.mjs accepts PORT other than 3000 but does not extend HOGEE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, so the route.ts Host guard refuses every API request on that port (fails closed).

**h-search**

- assembleWebSearch keys sanctionsHit and drafts by supplierId (Map, last wins) and storeWebSuppliers inserts first-wins, with no uniqueness check; parseTavilyBody de-duplicates by canonical href but supplier ids are only 60 bits of sha256 (supplier-w + 12 base32), so two attacker URLs with a birthday collision (~2^30 hashes) in one answer would share a sanctions verdict and a card name. Downstream webCandidateOf/screenTermsNames fail closed, but assembleWebSearch should omit duplicate ids and the id could carry more bits.
- priceFlag's median includes gate-excluded listings and the landed_cost anchor (cheapest) includes flagged bait prices, so a few untrusted listings can flag a legitimate cheaper listing as bait or push a flagged bait listing to rank 1. Consider computing the median over gate-passing listings and excluding priceFlag'd listings from the cheapest anchor.
- storeReady (web-search.ts) publishes READY without a deadline/staleness guard, so a search that readWebSearch already reported FAILED (PENDING > 120 s) can later flip to READY; add created_at > now() - PENDING_STALE_S to its update.
- The search-wide 45 s deadline means one slow listing (long Reader output plus a repair turn) can push the whole search to PROVIDER_DOWN; a per-listing Reader timeout that omits that listing would keep one listing from failing the search.
- listingTextOf keeps C0 controls including U+0000; Postgres jsonb rejects \u0000, so any listing-derived string that reached result_json or record_json (e.g. a Reader-grounded certificate name) would make storeReady fail the whole search. Strip \p{Cc} (except newline) when cleaning listing text.
- webCandidates() (web-candidates.ts) runs searchJob and scoreWebAnswer without SearchLimits, the daily cap or the budget headroom check; it has no production caller today, but a future caller would bypass the search limits. Remove it or route it through startWebSearch.
- Insert-only web supplier rows fix the first reading ever stored for a listing URL in that facility; a misread or renamed listing then stays TERMS_CANDIDATE for that supplier permanently (declared limit 4, fails closed but is a per-supplier denial).

**h-signing**

- packages/api/src/services/signing/supplier-approval.ts recheckAtCommit calls supplierLimits, which reads policyWorld and the open-order sum through pool(deps.db) rather than the transaction client q, while the transaction already holds a pool connection and the supplier-terms advisory lock. The result is still correct under READ COMMITTED (the lock is released only after the earlier commit is visible), but the lock holder needs extra pool connections; if concurrent confirmOrderTerms calls (anonymous founder persona, identical bodies are not counted by MAX_TERMS_PER_WINDOW) fill the pool while queued on the same lock, the commit stalls until a pool timeout. Pass q through supplierLimits/policyWorld for the commit-time recheck.
- packages/api/src/services/signing/supplier-approval.ts planOrder (catalog) computes free = allocated - spent - escrowed without subtracting open escrow orders and without the supplier-terms lock, so a catalog order signed after an open (unfunded) web order can promise budget the web order already holds; supplierLimits' stated invariant (two orders never promise the same budget) therefore holds only web-vs-web and catalog-before-web. Chain funding caps remain the backstop and the founder signs both orders; reuse supplierLimits and the lock in planOrder.
- packages/api/src/services/signing/web-order.ts webOrderRows puts the free-text holderName (2-120 chars) and bankName (2-80 chars), both typed in the terms form by any founder-persona caller in demo mode, in the same 'Pays out to' value as the grouped account digits. Both may contain digits and phrases such as 'simulated payout account 1002 0030 0400', so the panel can show a second, decoy account number before the real one. Render the account number in its own row and refuse digit runs or the fixed phrase in holder and bank names; how the sign dialog renders the value is the peer sign-dialog unit's boundary.
- A bindPayee that reverts after commit (for example SignatureExpired when the founder submits near the 900 s expiry and the relay lands later) leaves payees.status = PENDING forever (apps/worker/src/jobs/sync.ts only promotes bound payees; no writer sets CANCELLED in apps/worker/src or packages/api/src). Besides blocking the web supplier (declared limit 3), supplierLimits keeps subtracting that order's unfunded milestones, so the free SUPPLIER pocket for later web terms shrinks permanently (fail-closed). Refuse submits with too little expiry margin, and mark the payee CANCELLED when its bindPayee action is REVERTED.
- packages/core/src/search/assemble.ts sets the card displayName to cardSafeName(sellerName) (possibly '(name hidden)' or trimmed) while the hashed RankedSupplier.displayName and Supplier.displayName keep the raw Reader name; planWebOrder shows the card name in the title and Supplier row but matches and screens the raw name. Not exploitable on its own (the founder types the holder, and both names come from the same listing), but the signed panel can name a supplier differently from the name that was screened.

**h-terms**

- packages/api/src/services/supplier-terms.ts:45 rejects only \p{Cf} in holderName/bankName, and FormText (packages/core/src/schemas/orders.ts:50) rejects only C0/DEL. C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F), U+2028/U+2029 (mandatory line breaks) and blank-rendering letters (Hangul fillers U+115F/U+1160/U+3164/U+FFA0) are accepted, and both strings are rendered next to the grouped account number in the signed 'Pays out to' row (web-order.ts:153). Reuse sanctions.ts INVISIBLE plus \p{Cc}, \p{Zl} and \p{Zp}.
- bankName is free text (2-80 chars), is not sanctions-screened, and sits in the signed display row right before 'simulated payout account <digits>'. A string such as 'X Bank, simulated payout account 1234 5678 ...' can imitate the account field (bank name is outside quoteHash, declared limit 5). Constrain the bank name to a plain-name pattern, or show it in its own row.
- terms-names.ts distinctiveWords counts any Latin token of 3 or more letters, so common pinyin syllables ('xin', 'hua', 'tai', 'jia') or common English words ('sun', 'star') let an unrelated company holder match a seller (e.g. 'Hua Co' matches 'Ningbo Xin Hua Houseware Co Ltd'). Consider a minimum length or a common-syllable list. This matters only for a third party who is not the listing author.
- terms-candidate.ts webCandidateOf does not bind the stored search spec (productCategory, buyFrom) to the CURRENT committed plan. After a replan, a READY web search from the previous plan stays orderable for up to 7 days, and its category gates (e.g. MISSING_CERT for drinkware) were computed for the old category. Compare search.spec with committedSearchSpec at confirm/prepare/finalize.
- Two supplierLimits derivations exist: terms-checks.ts (allocated-spent-escrowed-open orders) for enforcement, and journey/effects.ts (pocket.availableMinor, no open-order subtraction) for preset display. They can disagree, so a preset shown as fitting is refused at confirm. This is display only, but one shared function would avoid the drift.
- Registry ids written in a listing earn scorer points when they are only well-formed (USCC check character, UEN/SSM format). A listing author can copy any real company's USCC to raise rank. The id is not bound to the seller name (documented as 'not proof that the entity exists'). Consider showing it as a claim only, or not scoring it for web candidates.

**h-web**

- SupplierApproval signing panel (apps/web/components/sign/what-you-sign.tsx:32-66, apps/web/lib/signed-rows.ts:87-98): for a web order, the verified rows show the payout account, schedule and quote only as fingerprints. The holder name, the full account number ('Pays out to', packages/api/src/services/signing/web-order.ts:153) and the milestone amounts appear only in the server description, which is collapsed in a closed <details> labelled 'not part of what you sign'. Builder-declared limit 1 ('the full account number is shown in the signed panel') is therefore weaker than stated: the founder must open an unsigned section, and the browser cannot check it against payoutAccountHash or scheduleHash. No lower-trust principal can split the two, because planWebOrder binds both to one row (web-order.ts:64-76). Fix: return the account preimage {channel, accountNumber, holderName} and the schedule in the signing response, recompute payoutAccountHash (JCS keccak, core payoutAccountPreimage) and scheduleHash in typed-data.ts, and show them as open, verified rows.
- apps/web/components/sign/sign-dialog.tsx:96-101: submit() awaits queryClient.invalidateQueries() while the requestSignature query is still enabled (open && ...), so every successful signature triggers a fresh requestSignature POST and a new server-side signing request that is never used (canSign is false once action is set). Not exploitable, but it adds pending request rows and changes `req` under the done panel. Fix: enabled: open && !action, or exclude the 'requestSignature' key from the invalidation.
- apps/web/components/chat/cards/search-view.ts:117 returns u.href, which keeps any query string or fragment, while the server promises origin + path only (allowedListingUrl). Return `${u.origin}${u.pathname}` for parity, so a future server regression cannot carry tracking or redirect parameters to the listing host.
- apps/web/next.config.ts sets only frame-ancestors in its CSP. No HTML or script sink was found for web-derived strings, so this has no current impact; a script-src/object-src policy would contain any future rendering regression.

**h-websearch**

- packages/checks/src/websearch.ts cleanText (122-125) strips data: URIs and markdown images in a single pass, so nested forms survive: '!![x](y)[a](https://h/p.png)' leaves '![a](https://h/p.png)' and 'da![x](y)ta:,AAAA' leaves 'data:,AAAA' (listingTextOf's second cleanText peels one more level only). Impact today is nil (the text only feeds the gate and the Reader, is never stored or rendered), but repeating the two replacements to a fixed point (bounded, e.g. 3 rounds) would make the stated invariant hold.
- packages/checks/src/websearch.ts cleanText caps at max*4 BEFORE NFKC (123) and runs both regex passes on the NFKC result, which can be up to 18x longer (U+FDFA); for raw_content that is ~864k chars per field before the final 12k cap. Work stays bounded (tens of millions of regex steps per field at worst, rate-limited to 20 searches/day), but re-capping to max*4 after normalize('NFKC') would tighten CPU per search.
- packages/api/src/services/eval-case.ts webSearchVerdict (228) re-derives gates via FLAG_SUPPLIER_GATE (PAYMENT_REDIRECT -> null) instead of core textGates/textPreGate (assemble.ts:116-129, PAYMENT_REDIRECT -> OFF_PLATFORM_DISCOUNT) and skips coreWebAnswer's Host drop. The eval is conservative (it under-reports exclusions) but can drift from the shipped gates it claims to mirror; calling core textPreGate would keep E1 numbers faithful.
- packages/api/src/services/web-candidates.ts fxRates (166-178) queries BNM for every distinct Reader-extracted offer currency, which is only checked against /^[A-Z]{3}$/ (assemble.ts:147, primitives.ts:182), and does not pass the 45 s search signal into getFx. Listing authors can therefore make each search issue up to ~10 codes x 8 look-back dates x 3 attempts of BNM GETs (bounded by the 20/day facility limit). Restricting offer currencies to ISO 4217 / the pack's supported list before FX, and honouring the search deadline, would remove the amplification.
- packages/checks/src/websearch.ts TAVILY_TARGET.maxBytes (69): the 2 MiB cap is per whole answer, so one ranked listing whose extracted raw_content is very large fails the entire live search (PROVIDER_DOWN, fail-closed by design). Whether Tavily truncates raw_content per result is a provider fact; owner check: inspect a live answer's per-result raw_content sizes. If unbounded, consider include_raw_content limits or a per-result cap at the provider.
- packages/checks/src/websearch.ts doc drift: comments and the CheckInputError text say 'at most 8' / '1-8 results' (5-7, 48, 177, 207) while WEB_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS and core WebSearchQuery allow 10; candidate cards are separately capped at 8 (assemble.ts:301). Not a security issue; align the text.
- Web supplier ids keep 60 bits (12 base32 chars of sha256, websearch.ts:155 / candidate.ts:83). A targeted second preimage (~2^60 SHA-256) only yields an insert-only id clash that fails closed as TERMS_CANDIDATE (declared limit 4); a longer id would remove even that.
